u0: Nothing is pending: no client has been left waiting for attention, no prepared food has been promised to a client, and no fallen food is awaiting pickup. From here the work is to respond to whatever comes next: a newly arrived client must have their order taken, fetched food must eventually be prepared and served, and any fallen food must be picked up on the very next step.
u1: An order has been taken, so that client is waiting and the taken order must still be followed by preparing food at the stove and then serving it. The order of fetching and preparing remains to be done. If food slips during this work, it must be picked up on the immediately following step.
u10: A new client has arrived and still needs to have their order taken, while an earlier order already has food prepared and awaiting delivery. The new order must be taken and the prepared portion served, with any slip recovered on the next step.
u11: A new client has arrived and needs their order taken, and the food has just slipped from the hands while a previous order is outstanding. The fallen food must be picked up on the very next step, then prepared and served alongside handling the new client.
u12: A prepared portion is being carried and must be delivered to the waiting client. Any slip of it must be answered by picking it up on the immediately next step; if it cannot be recovered then, the task can no longer succeed.
u13: Food has just slipped out of the hands while a prepared portion was still owed to a waiting client, and no order is currently taken. The food must be picked up on the very next step, then served; failing to regain it immediately makes success impossible.
u14: A mandatory requirement has been broken: food that slipped was not picked up on the very next step, or carried food was lost without being regained immediately. Successful completion is no longer possible.
u15: A client has just arrived and their order must be taken next, and there is also a prepared portion still to be delivered to a waiting client. If the carried food slips, it must be picked up on the immediately following step, or the task fails.
u16: Food has just slipped out of the hands while both a new client's order and a pending prepared serve are outstanding. The fallen food must be picked up on the very next step; otherwise success becomes impossible.
u2: The carried food has been prepared at the stove, so it must still be delivered to the waiting client. Because a client's order was necessarily taken before preparation, that client is still owed a serve. Any slip during this errand must be recovered on the very next step.
u3: Food has just slipped out of the hands while an order was already taken, so the client's order still needs preparing and serving. Picking the fallen food back up on the very next step is required, and failing to do so ends the task in failure.
u4: Food has just slipped out of the hands and an order is outstanding, so the client still needs preparation and serving of food. The slip must be answered by picking the food back up on the very next step; leaving the hands empty then makes success impossible.
u5: Food has just slipped out of the hands while food was already prepared, so the prepared portion must be regained and delivered to the client. The fallen food must be picked up on the immediately next step, or the task fails for good.
u6: A client has just arrived and their order has not been taken yet. The immediate job is to take that order, after which food must be fetched, prepared at the stove and served; any slip along the way must be recovered on the very next step.
u7: A client has just arrived and still needs to place an order, and separately a prepared portion is being carried that must be delivered to a waiting client. Both the new client's order and the pending serve remain outstanding, and any slip of the carried food must be recovered on the very next step.
u8: A client has just arrived and the food has just slipped out of the hands, with an order already taken by that client. The food must be picked up on the immediately next step, then prepared and served to the waiting client.
u9: A client has just arrived and the food has just slipped out of the hands, while food had already been prepared for a waiting client. The fallen food must be retrieved on the very next step, then delivered; both the new client's order and the pending serve remain.
